prompt.context: Our client, Seasoned Investors (SI), is a private equity firm that has just launched a new fund focused on investments in the food industry. For their first investment, they are considering acquiring Favored Flavors (FF), a spice company specializing in premium organic spices. Favored Flavors is asking for $75M, and the offer is final.
prompt.question: Should Seasoned Investors pursue this acquisition?

clarifying_info.q: What return does SI need from this investment?
clarifying_info.a: SI seeks a Multiple of Invested Capital (MOIC) of 2x — it seeks to earn double the value of its investment by the end of the holding period.

clarifying_info.q: How long will SI hold the investment?
clarifying_info.a: The fund has a holding period of 4 years, at which point the fund will sell the business.

clarifying_info.q: At what multiple will SI sell the business?
clarifying_info.a: SI is confident they will be able to sell the business at 10x EBITDA at the end of the holding period.
FF does not have any debt.
FF sells primarily to grocery store wholesalers.

clarifying_info.q: Does SI have experience in this space?
clarifying_info.a: A couple of SI managing directors have significant experience in this industry, but SI does not currently have any other portfolio companies in the food/beverage market.

exhibits.title: 2020 Income Statement and Industry Comparison
exhibits.shows: FF's 2020 income statement (Revenue, COGS, SG&A as % of revenue, EBITDA, Free Cash Flow as % of EBITDA) alongside an industry average cost breakdown pie chart showing EBIT, COGS components (Raw Materials, Packaging), Depreciation & Amortization, Labor, Marketing, R&D, and Other.

data.industry_COGS_note: Industry average COGS breakdown: 90% raw material, 10% packaging

exhibits.shows: A stacked bar chart showing revenue ($50M) and cost ($33M) broken down by spice product: Black Pepper, Cloves, Coriander, Cumin, Oregano, Paprika, Saffron, Sage, Thyme, Other, and Packaging. Each bar segment is labeled with a percentage for both revenue and cost.

Revenue_$50M_breakdown_pct.Packaging_note: not shown separately on revenue side

exhibits.title: Projected Revenue Growth
exhibits.shows: A bar chart of projected revenue ($M) from 2020 to 2024.

framework: Company — Profitability/Cash Flow Analysis: Revenue (price x quantity), COGS (variable: raw materials, packaging, shipping; fixed: manufacturing plant, labor), SG&A; Company leadership and capabilities
Valuation — Cash flow during holding period; Exit value (EBITDA multiple); Market growth and size
Market — Competition; Trends (ESG: fair wages/ethical sourcing/sustainability; customer trends: exotic foods, healthier eating, online grocery); Regulations (trade restrictions, import/export)

PE Firm — Fund objectives and restrictions; Synergies/improvements (future bolt-on acquisitions, investment-light revenue growth, cost optimization, firm industry expertise); Financing the acquisition; Exit strategy

questions.prompt: What insights do you draw from Exhibit 1 (FF's 2020 income statement and industry comparison)?
questions.guidance: FF's EBITDA margin is 10% ($5M / $50M), which is 4% below the industry average of 14% (EBIT 11% + D&A 3%). FF's COGS ratio is 66% ($33M/$50M), 8% higher than the industry average — possibly due to premium spice quality but may signal optimization opportunities. FF's SG&A at 23% is 4% below the industry average, a potential competitive advantage. Candidates should drive the case forward by asking for more detail on COGS breakdown.

steps: FF COGS % = 33 / 50 = 66%; Industry COGS roughly 58% implied (14% EBITDA gap)
FF SG&A % = (50 - 33 - 5) / 50 = 12 / 50 = 24% — note: case states 23% implying slight rounding; industry avg SG&A ~27%
math.answer: FF EBITDA margin 10% vs industry 14%; COGS 66% vs industry lower; SG&A 23% below industry average

questions.prompt: What insights do you draw from Exhibit 2 (Product Mix)? What cost optimization opportunities exist?
questions.guidance: Two key findings: (1) Packaging cost is 16% of total cost, vs industry average of 10% — an 6% gap representing potential savings. (2) Saffron is losing money: revenue = 5% of $50M = $2.5M; cost = 9% of $33M = ~$3M (round to $3M). The team believes Saffron cost can be reduced by 1/3. Candidates should calculate total EBITDA improvement and updated FCF.

math.setup: Packaging savings: (16% - 10%) * $33M. Saffron cost reduction: 9% * (1/3) * $33M. New EBITDA and FCF.
steps: New EBITDA: $5M + $3M = $8M (16% of $50M — now above industry average)
math.answer: Packaging savings ~$2M; Saffron cost reduction ~$1M; Total $3M improvement. New EBITDA = $8M (16%); New FCF = $5M (10% of revenue).

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 3 (Revenue Projections), calculate the total projected value of the business over the holding period. Does the acquisition meet SI's 2x MOIC requirement?
questions.guidance: Candidates should apply the new EBITDA margin (16%) and FCF margin (10% of revenue) to each year's projected revenue to compute annual FCFs, then calculate the exit value at 10x EBITDA in 2024, and sum everything. The total should be $154.50M vs the 2x MOIC threshold of $150M ($75M * 2). No discounting is needed — MOIC does not involve time value of money.

math.setup: Annual FCF = Revenue * 10%. Exit Value (2024) = Revenue_2024 * 16% * 10x. Total Value = Sum of FCFs (2021-2024) + Exit Value.
math.answer: Total projected value = $154.5M, which exceeds the 2x MOIC requirement of $150M. SI should proceed with the acquisition.

brainstorming.prompt: What risks should SI consider before proceeding with this acquisition?

categories.name: Market / Competitive Risks
ideas: Increased competition from other premium spice brands
Market growth may slow or reverse
Commodity price volatility for raw spice materials

categories.name: ESG / Regulatory Risks
ideas: Trade restrictions or import/export regulations on spice sourcing
Reputational risk if sourcing practices are not ethically verified

categories.name: Operational Risks
ideas: Revenue projections may not materialize — growth assumptions could be too optimistic
Cost reductions (packaging, Saffron) may be harder or slower to realize than modeled
Integration challenges if SI has limited operational control

categories.name: PE Firm / Deal Risks
ideas: Exit multiple may be lower than 10x EBITDA if market conditions change
Difficulty finding a buyer at the assumed exit price
No other food/beverage portfolio companies limits cross-portfolio synergies

recommendation: Seasoned Investors should proceed with the acquisition of Favored Flavors at $75M.

The projected total value of $154.5M exceeds the 2x MOIC requirement of $150M ($75M * 2), driven by $26.5M in cumulative free cash flows over the 4-year holding period and a $128M exit value at 10x EBITDA.
risks: Revenue growth projections may be optimistic; slower growth would reduce FCFs and compress the exit multiple
Cost optimization gains (packaging normalization, Saffron restructuring) may take time or face operational hurdles
Market or regulatory changes (trade restrictions, ESG compliance costs) could pressure margins
Exit conditions in 4 years are uncertain — a 10x EBITDA multiple is not guaranteed
next_steps: Validate revenue growth assumptions with market research and customer concentration analysis
Develop a detailed cost optimization plan for packaging and the Saffron product line
Assess potential bolt-on acquisition targets in the food/beverage space to accelerate growth
Conduct full due diligence on supply chain, sourcing contracts, and regulatory compliance
